rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi praises the Qur'an's inimitable concision, eloquence and wisdom, its ordered blend of literal and figurative speech, and its varied rhetorical forms and shifts of tone.
rows.anchor: وتظافر إيجازه وإعجازه ، وتظافرت حقيقته ومجازه ، وتقارن في الحسن مطالعه ومقاطعه

rows.speaker: أبو شامة
rows.claim: Abu Shama interprets the provision of the Lord as the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أبو شامة فى المرشد الوجيز فى قوله تعالى ﴿ ورزق ربك خير وأبقى ﴾ قال يعنى القرآن

rows.speaker: السخاوى
rows.claim: Al-Sakhawi says the Qur'an granted to the Prophet is better than the worldly provision given to others.
rows.anchor: وقال السخاوى يعنى ما رزقك الله من القرآن خير مما رزقهم من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi classifies declarative clauses as a type of sūra opening, listing al-Anbiya, al-Qamar and al-Rahman among twenty-three such sūras.
rows.anchor: الرابع الجمل الخبرية نحو ﴿ يسألونك عن الأنفال ﴾ ﴿ براءة من الله ﴾

words: لا هن حل لهم ولا هم يحلون لهن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition has two benefits: the prohibition may be bilateral although the impediment comes from one party, and the nominal clause states an established ruling while the future verb looks ahead.
rows.anchor: وللتكرار هنا فائدتان إحداهما أن التحريم قد يكون في الطرفين ولكن يكون المانع من إحداهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After affirmative speech, bal either retracts a mistaken human statement or moves to what is more apt; in divine speech it refutes human claims or marks a prior matter as past and shifts to what deserves mention.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن بل إذا ذكرت بعد كلام موجب فمعناها الإضراب وهو أما أن يقع في كلام الخلق ومعناه إبطال ما سبق

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik claims every Qur'anic bal begins a new purpose rather than retracting; Zarkashi rejects this, citing bal's explicit refutation of the claim that God took a son.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن مالك في شرح الكافية أن بل حيث وقعت في القرآن النرآن فإنها للاستئناف لغرض آخر لإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Lot's people's reply, bal turns from their pursuing males and abandoning wives to the judgment that they are transgressors.
rows.anchor: أضرب بها عن حقيقة إتيانهم الذكور وترك الأزواج

words: وأشهدوا ذوي عدل منكم وأقيموا الشهادة لله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first address in the witness instruction is to divorcing husbands and the next to witnesses; in the other example, the address shifts from husbands to guardians.
rows.anchor: فالأول للمطلقين والثاني للشهود نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the repeated contrasts between blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead as repetition of comparisons.
rows.anchor: ومنه تكرار الأمثال كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Number predicates omit an initial pronoun, understood as they are three, five or seven; in the two-party example, one party is understood from the mention of another.
rows.anchor: أي هم ثلاثة وهم خمسة وهم سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In bal ʿibād mukramūn, the omitted subject is hum: they are honored servants.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ بل عباد مكرمون ﴾ 4 أي هم عباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāgh fa-hal yahlik is read with an omitted subject: this is a message or warning.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ بلاغ فهل يهلك ﴾ 3 أي هذا بلاغ

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali supplies an omitted subject before the fire: it is the fire.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي قوله تعالى ﴿ بشر من ذلكم النار ﴾ 5 أي هي النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi also allows al-nār to be a subject whose following clause is its predicate; in the second example it may instead be apposition to evil punishment.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون النار في الآيتين مبتدأ والخبر الجملة التي بعدها ويمكن في الثانية أن تكون النار بدلا من سوء العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In these reports of opponents' words, the subject pronoun he is omitted before the predicate or accusation.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ فقالوا ساحر كذاب ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qul al-haqq means this is the truth from your Lord, with a demonstrative subject omitted; it does not mean say a true statement, which would put al-haqq in the accusative.
rows.anchor: فإنه لو أريد هذا لنصب الحق والمراد إثبات أن القرآن حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah anzalnāhā means this is a sūrah sent down, with the demonstrative omitted.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ سورة أنزلناها ﴾ 7 أي هذه سورة

words: من عمل صالحا فلنفسه ومن أساء فعليها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clauses mean that a person's good deed is for him and his bad deed is against him, with the deed nouns understood.
rows.anchor: أي فعمله لنفسه وإساءته عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other omitted-subject examples mean he is despairing, their roaming is a small enjoyment (or that is a small enjoyment), and the Crusher is God's Fire.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإن مسه الشر فيؤوس قنوط ﴾ 9 أي فهو يئوس

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح بن جنى
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains that each spark is like a palace, since all the sparks together cannot be compared to one palace; the word qasr denotes a hide tent erected over property, and the comparison is supported by camel herds.
rows.anchor: فجماعاته إذن مثل الجمالات الصفر وكذلك الأول شررة منه كالقصر قاله أبو الفتح بن جنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section explains apparent negation where a description is incomplete or its result absent, so wording denies the full or beneficial state rather than every outward act.
rows.anchor: لأنه عدم كمال وصفه أو لانتفاء ثمرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned are denied death because theirs is not real death, and denied life because it is neither good nor beneficial life.
rows.anchor: فنفي عنه الموت لأنه ليس بموت صريح ونفى عنه الحياة لأنها ليست بحياة طيبة ولا نافعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People at the Resurrection seem drunk from terror, though they are not drunk from wine.
rows.anchor: أي ما هم بسكارى مشروب ولكن سكارى فزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned do speak, as their plea shows, but because their speech brings no benefit it is treated as if they had not spoken.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم لما نطقوا بما لم ينفع فكأنهم لم ينطقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lists hearts that do not understand and the damned wishing they had listened or reasoned as further figurative denials of useful faculties.
rows.anchor: لهم قلوب لا يفقهون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mu'tazilites use the idols' apparent looking without sight to deny seeing God; Zarkashi rejects the inference: they only seem to look, and naẓar can mean supposing or knowing, so sight does not follow from the idols' lifeless gaze.
rows.anchor: فإن المعتزلة احتجوا به على نفى الرؤية لأن النظر لا يستلزم الإبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also lists fighting the leaders of disbelief because they have no binding oaths as an example of this rhetorical pattern.
rows.anchor: ومنه ﴿ فقاتلوا أئمة الكفر إنهم لا أيمان لهم ﴾ 1

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki and others say the initial oath-emphasized statement affirms their knowledge, then knowledge is denied because they do not act on it.
rows.anchor: كذا قاله السكاكي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says affirmation and negation do not concern the same thing: knowledge is affirmed but acting by it denied; similarly, the throwing's effect is denied while the act itself is affirmed.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال لم يتوارد النفي والإثبات على محل واحد لأن المثبت أولا نفس العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can mean substitution: preferring worldly life over the next, wealth not replacing God's obedience or mercy, and protection in place of the Merciful.
rows.anchor: أي بدلا من الآخرة ومحلها مع مجرورها النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can carry the sense of ʿalā in the statement that Noah was supported against his people; an alternative supplies a verb meaning that God prevented them through victory.
rows.anchor: السابع بمعنى على نحو ﴿ ونصرناه من القوم ﴾ 1 أي على القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi lists min in the two phrases about hearts hardened from God's remembrance and being unaware of this as meaning ʿan, about or away from.
rows.anchor: الثامن بمعنى عن نحو ﴿ فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative analysis takes min in both phrases as marking the starting point.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي للابتداء فيهما وقوله

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh indicates that min in God's feeding them from hunger can carry the sense of ʿan.
rows.anchor: فقد أشار سيبويه إلى إن من هنا تؤدي معنى عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative treats min as causal, equivalent to lām because of hunger; Zarkashi rejects this, saying the causal sense comes from ajl, not min.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي بمنزلة اللام للعلة أي لأجل الجوع وليس بشىء

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar chooses min here as marking the starting point.
rows.anchor: واختار الصفار أنها لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus, as cited by al-Baghawi, takes min in looking with a furtive glance as equivalent to bāʾ.
rows.anchor: التاسع بمعنى الباء نحو ﴿ ينظرون من طرف خفي ﴾ 5 حكاه البغوي عن يونس

rows.speaker: ابن أبان
rows.claim: Ibn Aban analyzes min in God's guardianship phrase as equivalent to bāʾ, meaning by God's command.
rows.anchor: وجعل منه ابن أبان ﴿ يحفظونه من أمر الله ﴾ 6 أي بأمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also lists min in salām min kulli amr as equivalent to bāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقوله ﴿ من كل أمر سلام ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min can mean fī, as in the call on Friday and asking what creatures made from the earth, or it can introduce a genus.
rows.anchor: العاشر بمعنى في نحو ﴿ إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة ﴾

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd takes min in the phrase about wealth and children not helping against God as meaning with or at God; another view reads it as substitution.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر بمعنى عند نحو ﴿ لن تغني عنهم أموالهم ولا أولادهم من الله ﴾ 2 قال أبو عبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min also separates opposites, as in distinguishing corrupter from reformer and impure from good.
rows.anchor: الثاني عشر بمعنى الفصل وهي الداخلة بين المتضادين نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basran grammarians require extra min to precede an indefinite and occur in negation, prohibition or a question; some treat a positive conditional clause like negation.
rows.anchor: الثالث عشر الزائدة ولها شرطان عند البصريين إن تدخل على نكرة وأن يكون الكلام نفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pause at man baʿathanā min marqadinā and begin this is what the Merciful promised, since some take the latter words as the angels' speech.
rows.anchor: يستحب الوقف على قوله ﴿ من بعثنا من مرقدنا ﴾ ثم يبتدىء فيقول ﴿ هذا ما وعد الرحمن ﴾ لأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A slight pause after qāla prevents mistaking God's name for the subject of the verb: Jacob is the speaker.
rows.anchor: فيقف على قال وقفة لطيفة لئلا يتوهم كون الاسم الكريم فاعل قال وإنما الفاعل يعقوب عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pause after the reassurance not to grieve over their words, then begin the statement that all might belongs to God.
rows.anchor: وكذا يجب الوقف على قوله ﴿ ولا يحزنك قولهم ﴾ ثم يبتدىء ﴿ إن العزة لله جميعا ﴾

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: Izz al-Din prefers a pause after ilaykumā: God's victory is through the signs and their qualities, with which Moses defeated the magicians, rather than the signs being something Pharaoh could not reach.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين الأحسن الوقف على ﴿ إليكما ﴾ لأن إضافة الغلبة إلى إلى الآيات أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pause after awalam yatafakkarū and begin mā biṣāḥibihim min jinnah to show the latter answers the charge that the Messenger is mad.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك يبين أنه رد لقول الكفار

rows.speaker: الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani calls the pause after awalam yatafakkarū complete.
rows.anchor: وقال الدانى إنه وقف تام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads those who differ as Jews and Christians and those spared as Muslims; God created them for His mercy, supporting a stop after the phrase about their creation.
rows.anchor: فإن ابن عباس قال في تفسير الآية ﴿ ولا يزالون مختلفين ﴾ يعني اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Separating the clauses clarifies that Joseph is told to overlook the offense, while the woman is ordered to seek forgiveness for her attempted sin; Joseph only meant to defend himself.
rows.anchor: لأن يوسف عليه السلام أمر بالأعراض وهو الصفح عن جهل من جهل قدره وأراد ضره

rows.speaker: الداني
rows.claim: Al-Dani calls the pause after wa-laqad hammat bihi and before wa-hamma bihā adequate; another view calls it complete.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الدانى إنه كاف وقيل تام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain Joseph's intention as an omitted aim, namely to push her away; this reading separates the two reports and parallels stopping at li-nubayyina lakum before beginning wa-nuqirru in 22:5.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أنه على حذف مضاف أي هم بدفعها وعلى هذا فالوقف على ﴿ همت به ﴾ كالوقف

words: لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some treat renewed explicit subjects as proof of a new sentence, but Zarkashi argues that examples such as wa-nuqirru are resumptive because coordination would require different verb forms; he likewise treats wayamḥu and al-rāsikhūn as resumptive.
rows.anchor: قلت وكثير من هذا لا يرد عليهم فان كلامهم في الواو العاطفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetoricians say no conjunction is needed when a following clause is so closely joined that it restates or emphasizes the first, as predicate, explanation or equivalent meaning.
rows.anchor: وقال البيانيون للجملة ثلاثة أحوال فالاول إن يكون ما قبلها بمنزلة الصفة من الموصوف والتاكيد من المؤكد فلا يدخلها عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the rebuke about turning away from the reminder, in makes the certain charge of excess sound conditional, as if it should have been absent.
rows.anchor: فاستعملت ان في مقام الجزم بكونهم مسرفين لتصور ان الاسراف ينبغي أن يكون منتفيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional challenges and stirs hearers: if they truly worship God, they must thank Him for His provision; this form also appears in argument and exhortation.
rows.anchor: والمعنى عبادتكم لله تستلزم شكركم له فان كنتم ملتزمين عبادته فكلوا من رزقه واشكروه

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In uses a conditional form to address everyone although only some doubt, since a universal address adopts the majority and doubt from those not doubting is treated as uncertain.
rows.anchor: فاستعمل ان مع تحقق الارتياب منهم لان الكل لم يكونوا مرتابين فغلب غير المرتابين منهم على المرتابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because in marks possibility, its answer normally uses the present; the past in waddu is purposeful because their desire for disbelief is certain, unlike the conditional future capture and hostility.
rows.anchor: فإن عدل عن المضارع إلى الماضي لم يعدل إلا لنكتة

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ
rows.speaker: صاحب البسيط
rows.claim: The Sahib al-Basit says apparent delay varies with the time an action takes; the sequence in the example allows for lengthy stages and so does not conflict with the sense of fa in a parallel account.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب البسيط طول المدة وقصرها بالنسبة إلى وقوع الفعل فيهما فإن كان الفعل يقتضي زمنا طويلا

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِن مُّضْغَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view distinguishes thumma, which looks to the beginning of the preceding event, from fa, which looks to its end, resolving why the same subject can take either particle.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قال لبعضهم ثم لملاحظة أول زمن المعطوف عليه والفاء لملاحظة آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer Izz al-Din's question about fa and thumma in return-and-accounting verses, Zarkashi says the Prophet's community is judged first and other peoples after; fa refers to the first group and thumma to completion.
rows.anchor: وأجاب بأن أول ما تحاسب أمة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم الأمم بعدهم فتحمل الفاء على أول المحاسبين

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi says thumma marks a longer interval than fa, so fa can allow delay; only later grammarians insist that it necessarily means immediate succession.
rows.anchor: نص الفارسي في الإيضاح على إن ثم أشد تراخيا من الفاء فدل على إن الفاء لها تراخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa can mark a difference in rank between the stages of arranging, driving and reciting, or between the ranks of the angelic groups in those acts.
rows.anchor: وتجىء لتفاوت ما بين رتبتين كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase fī-mā is written separately because people's desires differ or exist in distinct forms.
rows.anchor: وهو مفصول لأن شهوات الأنفس مختلفة أو مفصلة في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kailā is joined when negation covers a universal, since denying the whole also denies its parts; it is separated when it negates a particular, since denying a part does not negate the whole.
rows.anchor: وإنما يوصل حيث يكون حرف النفي دخل على معنى كلي فيوصل لأن نفي الكلي نفي لجميع جزئياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction depends on scope: min makes the time phrase general in the joined example but particular in the separated one; the other examples have one or more limiting conditions.
rows.anchor: لأن الظرف في هذا خاص الاعتبار وهو في الأول عام الاعتبار لدخول من عليه وهذا كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pronouns such as hum denote the named group as a whole without dividing it into separately existing parts; dividing the referent is only a mental abstraction.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك هم ونحوه من الضمائر تدل على جملة المسمى من غير تفصيل والإضمار حال لا صفة وجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says separating māl in script reflects the severed possessive connection: hypocrites separated harm from good in attributing events to God, and God will sever their tie with believers at Judgment.
rows.anchor: فقطعوا وصل السيئة بالحسنة في الإضافة إلى الله ففرقوا بينهما كما أخبر سبحانه والله قد وصل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lām can mark an outcome rather than an intended goal: Pharaoh's household took Moses up for the opposite reason, as their hope he might help them or be adopted shows.
rows.anchor: وتسمى لام العاقبة فإن من المعلوم أنهم لم يلتقطوه لذلك بل لضده بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purpose lām can contain an understood kay; kay can occur with lām or without it, and the passage gives examples of both purpose and outcome.
rows.anchor: ومثال لام كي وكي مضمرة معها قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba reports a proposed test for lām of consequence: it permits substituting fa in its place.
rows.anchor: وحكى ابن قتيبة عن بعضهم إن علامتها جواز تقدير الفاء موضعها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says lām expresses cause without requiring that the cause be an intended goal, as in leaving a town for fear of danger.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في تفسير سورة المدثر أفادت اللام نفس العلة والسبب ولا يجب في العلة إن تكون غرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarkashi distinguishes purpose lām, whose result is the agent's aim, from consequence lām, which indicates only an outcome.
rows.anchor: لكن الفرق بينها وبين لام التعليل التي في نحو قوله

rows.speaker: الأشعري
rows.claim: Ibn Furak transmits al-Ashʿari's view that every lām attributed to God expresses consequence rather than purpose, since God cannot have an aim.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن فورك عن الأشعري أن كل لام نسبها الله إلى نفسه فهي للعاقبة والصيرورة دون التعليل

rows.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
rows.claim: Izz al-Din objects with examples of explicit divine purpose; Zarkashi answers that such purpose is possible as an act of grace.
rows.anchor: واستشكله الشيخ عز الدين بقوله
